intro: A life spent moving between countries, languages, and disciplines — from military service to software to the flight line. Scroll through, or jump straight to any year.

chapters.title: Joining the Argentine Navy Reserve
chapters.text: Started as a reservist in the Argentine Navy, training in hazmat/dangerous goods handling, firefighting, and combat medic skills — a foundation of procedure and discipline that still shows up in how I approach ramp safety today.

chapters.title: Writing software for the first time professionally
chapters.text: Joined Brain Knowledge Systems in Argentina as a developer, working in Python, Django, and C. This is where the engineering side of things started — a thread that later became automation scripts, side projects, and eventually freelance work.

chapters.title: HR reporting at Accenture
chapters.text: Moved into HR report writing at Accenture Argentina, working with Workday. Less code, more data and process — but it sharpened how I think about structuring information clearly for other people to use.

chapters.title: Moving to Japan
chapters.text: Relocated to Sapporo, Hokkaido. New language environment, new career direction — the start of the aviation ground operations chapter.

chapters.title: Ramp agent at Skymark Airlines
chapters.text: Began working ramp and ground operations at New Chitose Airport — baggage handling, aircraft turnaround, and the procedural rhythm of airside work.

chapters.title: Ramp agent at FRS
chapters.text: Continued in ground operations at FRS, taking on weight and balance responsibilities alongside ramp safety work.

chapters.title: Building things on the side
chapters.text: Shipped a METAR/TAF weather app for pilots, built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, and started taking on freelance Python and automation work — bringing the software side back into the picture alongside aviation.
